findings.claim: The design sketch scans the global process.argv instead of the function's canonical args parameter, making the AC3 unconditional-precedence path unreachable through in-process invocation: runDeliveryJourney({ args: ['--version','--bogus'] }) would miss the pre-scan (the test runner's own argv lacks the token), fall into parseArgs, and exit 1 via the unknown-option catch, contradicting AC3's letter outside the real CLI. The retained post-parse 'if (options.version)' branch partially compensates but cannot handle the mixed invalid combination.
findings.evidence: delivery-journey.mjs:476 'export async function runDeliveryJourney({ args = process.argv.slice(2), ... })'; design.md sketch 'if (process.argv.includes(\'--version\') ) { ...; return 0; }' followed by a second 'if (options.version)' branch; parseArgs catch at delivery-journey.mjs:493-495 returns failInput for '--bogus'. For the real CLI the two scans are equivalent (node/script paths can never equal the token '--version'), so AC1-AC4 as written (CLI form) all hold.
findings.recommendation: Scan 'args' (the parameter) rather than the global process.argv — identical CLI behavior by the default binding, and the precedence mechanism becomes injection-testable; alternatively document why both the pre-scan and the post-parse fallback branch exist (the fallback is the in-process/unit-test path).

findings.claim: The option-value/-- boundary codex-agent asked to clarify is only half-addressed: the exact-token match settles '--version=<value>' (not the flag; parseArgs rejects a value on the boolean), but a '--' separator is not discussed — after the change, 'delivery-journey.mjs -- --version' prints the version instead of today's INVALID_INPUT. Immaterial in practice because the CLI accepts no positional arguments at all (parseArgs strict without allowPositionals rejects every positional, so no legitimate invocation ever carries '--version' as data).
findings.evidence: proposal.md AC3 'scans process.argv for the exact token --version'; design.md D1 same; codex-agent r1 F1 recommendation '明确选项值及 -- 分隔符的边界'; delivery-journey.mjs:479-492 declares no allowPositionals.
findings.recommendation: Add one sentence to D1/D3 stating the boundary explicitly: any exact '--version' token anywhere in argv wins, including after '--', which is safe because the tool has no positional surface; or make the pre-scan stop at '--' if strict GNU parity is preferred.

findings.claim: AC4's literal wording ('every other exit-path behavior is unchanged: unknown options other than --version are still INVALID_INPUT exit 1') read in isolation still contradicts AC3's combination case ('--bogus --version' now exits 0); design D3 carries the needed carve-out ('unknown-option rejection still applies to invocations WITHOUT --version') but AC4 itself does not.

summary: APPROVE. The r1 blocking finding (codex-agent F1: strict parseArgs fails before a post-parse short-circuit, so declared precedence was not guaranteed) is genuinely resolved by the r2 revision, verified against the pilot target file: delivery-journey.mjs:479-495 runs parseArgs with strict:true inside a try/catch that returns failInput (exit 1) on any unknown option, so only a scan placed BEFORE parsing can give --version unconditional precedence — exactly what revised AC3 and design D1/D3 now specify (process.argv exact-token pre-scan). With the pre-scan, --version combined with unknown options, mutex violations, or missing required args prints the bare version and exits 0 (AC1/AC3); unknown-option rejection and the whole 0/1/2 exit contract are preserved for argv without --version (AC4), and no filesystem side effect occurs (first mkdir is at line 520, far after the pre-scan; exit goes through the tool's process.exitCode entry at 1194-1196, per D4). The change stays inside the single mandated file plus one usage line, adds no I/O, env, or runtime version read (frozen constant), and the redundancy of also declaring the version option keeps an in-process degraded path. Remaining items are advisory: tasks.md was not updated to the pre-scan mechanism and still lacks a verification task (F1); the sketch scans global process.argv rather than the args parameter, leaving AC3's combination case untestable via in-process injection (F2); the '--'-separator boundary codex asked about is undocumented but immaterial for a positionals-free CLI (F3); AC4's wording needs the without---version carve-out that D3 already states (F4). All criteria are at or above 7.5 and I would authorize the next step now.
